config.classes_note: Three classes, each sourced by the field B and the census record: (1) computational and procedural poetry (B1, B2, B3, B4, B5, B7, B8; census kind and tll_reading, which names 'the procedural column of #186'); (2) literary magazines and journals of digital writing (B1, B4, B7, B8; census record_type, evidence_kind 'journal' and area 'field-history'); (3) writing under a size constraint (B2, B3, B8; census stated_limits). Aliases: the name (case-sensitive; the common noun 'taper' and its senses, which Wikipedia's disambiguation page lists, are read out at admission), the social handle and new domain taperzine, the old host, and the publisher's name Bad Quarto (case-sensitive; the Shakespearean 'bad quarto', a bibliographic term, is a homonym and is read out at admission). Nick Montfort (publisher, B4, B8), Angela Chang and Helen Shewolfe Tseng (editors, B2, B4, B8) and The Trope Tank at MIT (B4) are distinct entities and are not aliases. #186 and #1543, the census's anchors, are read at the passages that bear on the entity's kind: #186's division of the field by the direction of address, its procedural lineage (with Montfort named among its living masters) and its three criteria of address, architecture and persistence; #1543's claim of machine composition. The census's tll_reading applies #186's procedural column to the entity: that reading is the archive's, ledgered as TLL-NN. Admission by reading (§3.4): D where a deposit names the magazine and says something of it; R where it states a relation between the magazine and an archive object; O-class where a sentence applies an archive category (the direction of address, the machine as method or as reader, the three criteria) to one of the three classes; a bare mention, a citation line or a homonym is not a claim.
